python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import colorsys
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
W,H = im.size
px = im.load()
cols=[]
for x in range(W):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(H):
        p=px[x,y]; r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r/H,g/H,b/H))

def sat(c):
    mx,mn=max(c),min(c)
    return (mx-mn)

# global stats
import statistics
lum=[0.299*c[0]+0.587*c[1]+0.114*c[2] for c in cols]
print("mean luminance:", sum(lum)/len(lum))
print("min/max lum:", min(lum), max(lum))

# find saturated stripes
print("\n--- saturated / distinct color stripes (sat>40) ---")
runs=[]
cur=None
for x in range(W):
    c=cols[x]; s=sat(c)
    if s>40:
        if cur is None: cur=[x,x,c]
        else: cur[1]=x
    else:
        if cur: runs.append(cur); cur=None
if cur: runs.append(cur)
for a,b,c in runs:
    # average color of run
    rs=gs=bs=0
    for x in range(a,b+1):
        rs+=cols[x][0]; gs+=cols[x][1]; bs+=cols[x][2]
    n=b-a+1
    print(f"x={a:4d}-{b:4d} (len {n:3d}) avg=({rs/n:.0f},{gs/n:.0f},{bs/n:.0f})")
EOF

input.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image, ImageEnhance
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')

# brightness/gamma boost version to reveal detail
def boost(img, gamma=0.55):
    lut=[min(255,int(255*((i/255)**gamma))) for i in range(256)]*3
    return img.point(lut)

boost(im).resize((2000,400), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/barcode_boost.png')

# crops
im.crop((390,0,560,200)).resize((1020,600), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/crop_blue.png')
im.crop((460,0,560,200)).resize((600,600), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/crop_teal.png')
boost(im.crop((590,0,760,200))).resize((1020,600), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/crop_mid.png')
boost(im.crop((0,0,200,200))).resize((1200,600), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/crop_start.png')
boost(im.crop((820,0,1000,200))).resize((1080,600), Image.NEAREST).save('/tmp/crop_end.png')
print("saved")
EOF
ls -la /tmp/crop_*.png /tmp/barcode_boost.png

***The Warrior's Way*** is a 2010 New Zealand-South Korean [fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film") [action film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film") written and directed by Sngmoo Lee and starring [Jang Dong-gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jang_Dong-gun "Jang Dong-gun"), [Kate Bosworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bosworth "Kate Bosworth"), [Geoffrey Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Rush "Geoffrey Rush"), [Danny Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Huston "Danny Huston") and [Tony Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Cox_\(actor\) "Tony Cox (actor)"). The film was released on 3 December 2010\. Its plot concerns a 19th-century warrior named Yang ([Jang Dong-gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jang_Dong-gun "Jang Dong-gun")), who is ordered to kill the last member of an enemy clan — a baby girl. He refuses the mission and flees with the child to a dilapidated town in the [American West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_West "Old West").

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 19th century Asia, Yang is a warrior and member of Sad Flute's clan, the cruelest assassins in the east. His personal goal to become the greatest swordsman in the entire world is accomplished when he kills the former champion and leader of the enemy clan. Both clans having sworn to fight until every member of the opposing clan is dead, Yang has killed every member except a baby girl, deciding to spare her. This act makes Yang a sworn enemy of his own clan, and forces him to flee his homeland.

After making his way to the [American West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_West "American West"), Yang arrives in the small town of Lode. There he seeks out a fellow rogue warrior friend known to the townsfolk as Smiley, but he discovers that Smiley died 3 years previously. Among the townspeople Yang meets are a gang of carnival members led by the dwarf Eight-Ball, town drunk Ron and Lynne, a spunky young woman who was friends with Smiley.

Lynne gives Yang the nickname Skinny and agrees to teach him how to do the laundry. Naming the baby girl ‘April’, Yang begins to enjoy life in the town, learning to enjoy pleasures he never knew as a warrior, even finding an interest in opera after Lynne shows him a gramophone. Lynne reveals to Yang that Smiley taught her about using a sword and the Sad Flute clan, and she wants Yang to teach her more, but he is reluctant to do so. Back in the East, Yang's former master Saddest Flute and his warrior army board the same boat to America, killing the entire crew in the process.

Yang sees Lynne place flowers on a grave, and asks Eight-Ball what happened. He explains that when Lynne was a young girl, the town came under siege by a corrupt Colonel. His preference to rape women with healthy teeth prompted him to choose Lynne as his victim, but she was able to escape by throwing a pan of boiling grease in his face. She flees, but the Colonel shoots her in the back and kills her father, mother, and baby brother.

When the townsfolk buried her family, they found Lynne still breathing. Ever since, Lynne has sworn revenge against the Colonel. Lynne gives Yang a pendant as a gift after he teaches her how to throw knives.

Yang shows her his jedok geom (a Korean single-edged sword), but Lynne notes it is welded to its scabbard. Yang explains it is so he cannot fight any longer. In a flashback, Yang is shown being given a puppy by his master.

The Colonel returns to the town to terrorize the people, sporting a frightening mask to hide the grotesque scar from the hot grease. The Colonel tortures a clown by having his men shoot at a bucket of water on the Clown's head, and is about to shoot a glass of whiskey himself when Ron drinks it and is dragged through the town with a whip around his neck being pulled by a horse. The Colonel then inspects a lineup of women for their teeth, and chooses a Hispanic woman whose husband begs for mercy. The Colonel releases the woman to her husband, to only shoot them down simultaneously with a single bullet.

Eight-Ball and the other carnival members tie Lynne up in a cellar for her own safety and Yang removes her blades, but she manages to free herself with a knife hidden in her boot. The Colonel has the Hispanic woman's daughters cleaned to be raped, but Lynne, disguised as a prostitute, offers herself instead. She initially fools the Colonel before he reveals he remembers who she is. His men then rush in to hold Lynne down on the bed. Back in the laundry, the carnival members run in looking for Lynne, and Yang realises where she is. He grabs an iron and shatters the seal on his sword to free it. Far away, Saddest Flute jerks up from meditation, sensing the seal break.

Just as Lynne is about to be raped, Yang bursts in through the window and expertly slays everyone in the room except the Colonel. As Yang turns to kill him, Lynne intercedes, saying that she will do it, but the Colonel grabs her and leaps out the window, using her to break his fall before attempting to flee on horse, but Lynne is able to deliver an expert knife throw to his back. The townsfolk pull off the mask to reveal a decoy instead, and are terrified that the Colonel will return to kill them. Yang is about to leave town before the Sad Flutes come for him, but the townsfolk implore him to stay and help.

The people are worried they don't have the means to defend themselves, but Eight-Ball has Ron's secret stash of guns and explosives unburied. Ron is shown to be an expert marksman, shooting a bowling pin down amidst his best liquor from hundreds of feet away. Yang asks Ron why he stopped shooting and Ron explains that he was once an outlaw, using his great skill to rob banks and trains. His criminal career ended when the woman he loved was shot during a gunfight, and he vowed to never pick up a gun again. Ron advises Yang that the best thing he can do is stay far away from those he cares about. The day before battle, Lynne asks to leave with Yang. Later that night, Yang comes to Lynne's house and gives her his twin short swords.

The Colonel arrives with scores of outlaws to assault the town. As the men approach, they are met with explosions. Perched at the top of the [Ferris wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_wheel "Ferris wheel"), Ron is sniping sticks of dynamite hidden in the garden as riders come. In the ensuing dust and chaos, Yang rapidly and stealthily disposes of many of the men. The outlaws are lured to the Ferris wheel, where Yang and the carnival members ambush them as Ron slides to safety on a cable, and the Ferris wheel is blown up, killing many of the Colonel's men. The survivors chase the carnival members to the centre of town, where the Sad Flutes suddenly assemble. Yang looks to Lynne holding April and tells her to run.

Yang follows Lynne to the laundry shop, killing many warriors on the way as the outlaws and warriors engage in battle. In the laundry, Lynne hands April to Eight-Ball so she can help Yang. After they kill some warriors, they hear shots and run to the dying Eight-Ball, who says he couldn't protect April. The Colonel is then shown entering a building carrying April.

The Sad Flutes pursue, but are fended off with a machine gun. However, the outlaws are unable to stop Yang, who brutally slices through them as he chases after the Colonel. He enters a room to find the Colonel holding a gun to April's head, but leaps up to cut the gun barrel and bullet in half mid-firing. Catching April, Yang steps aside to let Lynne fight the Colonel. After a tense battle, Lynne manages to finally drive a sword into the Colonel's back.

Yang and Lynne exit the room to find Saddest Flute waiting, who tells Yang that April is the enemy, and asks if he would ever tell April that he killed her parents. Yang and Saddest Flute go to the desert at sunset and duel to the death. During the duel, flashbacks show Saddest Flute training Yang and forcing him to kill the puppy he was given, declaring Yang's biggest enemy would be his heart. In the present, Yang wins the duel, cutting Saddest Flute's throat.

Lynne tells Yang she knows she won't be coming with him, and tries to hand him April, but he refuses. He makes the baby laugh once more, and gives Lynne a caring look before turning to the sunset and leaving. Ron narrates that Yang never stopped walking, putting as much space between him and the people he loved as possible. The scene then shifts to a hooded man in a parka. Another man approaches and the hooded man nimbly kills him, knives falling out of the latter's hands as he collapses. The hooded man, revealed to be Yang, stands up and goes to his shack, where he takes the pendant he had been given by Lynne, his sword disguised as a snowman's broom and April's pacifier before setting the hut on fire. Walking out to the snow, a slew of clan warriors leap out of the snow, and Yang unsheathes his sword as the scene fades.

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast")\]

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

The film was written and directed by Sngmoo Lee, and produced by [Barrie M. Osborne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrie_M._Osborne "Barrie M. Osborne") (who also produced *[The Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_\(film_series\) "The Lord of the Rings (film series)")*[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)), along with Lee Joo-Ick and [Michael Peyser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Peyser "Michael Peyser"). [Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography") was by Woo-Hyung Kim, and Jonathan Woodford-Robinson edited the film. [Javier Navarrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Navarrete "Javier Navarrete") composed the score.

Filming began in [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland") on 12 November 2007 and wrapped on 28 February 2008\.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

The film received negative reviews. It has a 31% approval rating on the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 42 reviews, with an average rating of 4\.5 out of 10\. The website's consensus reads, "Perfectly, thoroughly divisive, *The Warrior's Way* will either be delightful or unbearable, depending on your tolerance for surreal, shamelessly over the top collisions of eastern and western clichés."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "C−" on an A+ to F scale.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")\]

In the film's opening weekend, it grossed a poor $3,048,665 in the US. The film ranked \#9 at the weekend charts.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The number of theatres dramatically reduced from 1,622 to 34 within three weeks from the opening day.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The film grossed $11,087,569 worldwide and had a production budget of $42 million, making the movie a [box office bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_office_bomb "Box office bomb").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The movie was one of the biggest box office bombs of 2010 next to *[MacGruber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacGruber_\(film\) "MacGruber (film)")*, *[How Do You Know](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_You_Know "How Do You Know")* and *[Jonah Hex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hex_\(film\) "Jonah Hex (film)")*.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

***The Warrior's Way*** is a 2010 New Zealand-South Korean [fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film") [action film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film") written and directed by Sngmoo Lee and starring [Jang Dong-gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jang_Dong-gun "Jang Dong-gun"), [Kate Bosworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bosworth "Kate Bosworth"), [Geoffrey Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Rush "Geoffrey Rush"), [Danny Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Huston "Danny Huston") and [Tony Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Cox_\(actor\) "Tony Cox (actor)"). The film was released on 3 December 2010\. Its plot concerns a 19th-century warrior named Yang ([Jang Dong-gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jang_Dong-gun "Jang Dong-gun")), who is ordered to kill the last member of an enemy clan — a baby girl. He refuses the mission and flees with the child to a dilapidated town in the [American West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_West "Old West").

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

In 19th century Asia, Yang is a warrior and member of Sad Flute's clan, the cruelest assassins in the east. His personal goal to become the greatest swordsman in the entire world is accomplished when he kills the former champion and leader of the enemy clan. Both clans having sworn to fight until every member of the opposing clan is dead, Yang has killed every member except a baby girl, deciding to spare her. This act makes Yang a sworn enemy of his own clan, and forces him to flee his homeland.

After making his way to the [American West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_West "American West"), Yang arrives in the small town of Lode. There he seeks out a fellow rogue warrior friend known to the townsfolk as Smiley, but he discovers that Smiley died 3 years previously. Among the townspeople Yang meets are a gang of carnival members led by the dwarf Eight-Ball, town drunk Ron and Lynne, a spunky young woman who was friends with Smiley.

Lynne gives Yang the nickname Skinny and agrees to teach him how to do the laundry. Naming the baby girl ‘April’, Yang begins to enjoy life in the town, learning to enjoy pleasures he never knew as a warrior, even finding an interest in opera after Lynne shows him a gramophone. Lynne reveals to Yang that Smiley taught her about using a sword and the Sad Flute clan, and she wants Yang to teach her more, but he is reluctant to do so. Back in the East, Yang's former master Saddest Flute and his warrior army board the same boat to America, killing the entire crew in the process.

Yang sees Lynne place flowers on a grave, and asks Eight-Ball what happened. He explains that when Lynne was a young girl, the town came under siege by a corrupt Colonel. His preference to rape women with healthy teeth prompted him to choose Lynne as his victim, but she was able to escape by throwing a pan of boiling grease in his face. She flees, but the Colonel shoots her in the back and kills her father, mother, and baby brother.

When the townsfolk buried her family, they found Lynne still breathing. Ever since, Lynne has sworn revenge against the Colonel. Lynne gives Yang a pendant as a gift after he teaches her how to throw knives.

Yang shows her his jedok geom (a Korean single-edged sword), but Lynne notes it is welded to its scabbard. Yang explains it is so he cannot fight any longer. In a flashback, Yang is shown being given a puppy by his master.

The Colonel returns to the town to terrorize the people, sporting a frightening mask to hide the grotesque scar from the hot grease. The Colonel tortures a clown by having his men shoot at a bucket of water on the Clown's head, and is about to shoot a glass of whiskey himself when Ron drinks it and is dragged through the town with a whip around his neck being pulled by a horse. The Colonel then inspects a lineup of women for their teeth, and chooses a Hispanic woman whose husband begs for mercy. The Colonel releases the woman to her husband, to only shoot them down simultaneously with a single bullet.

Eight-Ball and the other carnival members tie Lynne up in a cellar for her own safety and Yang removes her blades, but she manages to free herself with a knife hidden in her boot. The Colonel has the Hispanic woman's daughters cleaned to be raped, but Lynne, disguised as a prostitute, offers herself instead. She initially fools the Colonel before he reveals he remembers who she is. His men then rush in to hold Lynne down on the bed. Back in the laundry, the carnival members run in looking for Lynne, and Yang realises where she is. He grabs an iron and shatters the seal on his sword to free it. Far away, Saddest Flute jerks up from meditation, sensing the seal break.

Just as Lynne is about to be raped, Yang bursts in through the window and expertly slays everyone in the room except the Colonel. As Yang turns to kill him, Lynne intercedes, saying that she will do it, but the Colonel grabs her and leaps out the window, using her to break his fall before attempting to flee on horse, but Lynne is able to deliver an expert knife throw to his back. The townsfolk pull off the mask to reveal a decoy instead, and are terrified that the Colonel will return to kill them. Yang is about to leave town before the Sad Flutes come for him, but the townsfolk implore him to stay and help.

The people are worried they don't have the means to defend themselves, but Eight-Ball has Ron's secret stash of guns and explosives unburied. Ron is shown to be an expert marksman, shooting a bowling pin down amidst his best liquor from hundreds of feet away. Yang asks Ron why he stopped shooting and Ron explains that he was once an outlaw, using his great skill to rob banks and trains. His criminal career ended when the woman he loved was shot during a gunfight, and he vowed to never pick up a gun again. Ron advises Yang that the best thing he can do is stay far away from those he cares about. The day before battle, Lynne asks to leave with Yang. Later that night, Yang comes to Lynne's house and gives her his twin short swords.

The Colonel arrives with scores of outlaws to assault the town. As the men approach, they are met with explosions. Perched at the top of the [Ferris wheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_wheel "Ferris wheel"), Ron is sniping sticks of dynamite hidden in the garden as riders come. In the ensuing dust and chaos, Yang rapidly and stealthily disposes of many of the men. The outlaws are lured to the Ferris wheel, where Yang and the carnival members ambush them as Ron slides to safety on a cable, and the Ferris wheel is blown up, killing many of the Colonel's men. The survivors chase the carnival members to the centre of town, where the Sad Flutes suddenly assemble. Yang looks to Lynne holding April and tells her to run.

Yang follows Lynne to the laundry shop, killing many warriors on the way as the outlaws and warriors engage in battle. In the laundry, Lynne hands April to Eight-Ball so she can help Yang. After they kill some warriors, they hear shots and run to the dying Eight-Ball, who says he couldn't protect April. The Colonel is then shown entering a building carrying April.

The Sad Flutes pursue, but are fended off with a machine gun. However, the outlaws are unable to stop Yang, who brutally slices through them as he chases after the Colonel. He enters a room to find the Colonel holding a gun to April's head, but leaps up to cut the gun barrel and bullet in half mid-firing. Catching April, Yang steps aside to let Lynne fight the Colonel. After a tense battle, Lynne manages to finally drive a sword into the Colonel's back.

Yang and Lynne exit the room to find Saddest Flute waiting, who tells Yang that April is the enemy, and asks if he would ever tell April that he killed her parents. Yang and Saddest Flute go to the desert at sunset and duel to the death. During the duel, flashbacks show Saddest Flute training Yang and forcing him to kill the puppy he was given, declaring Yang's biggest enemy would be his heart. In the present, Yang wins the duel, cutting Saddest Flute's throat.

Lynne tells Yang she knows she won't be coming with him, and tries to hand him April, but he refuses. He makes the baby laugh once more, and gives Lynne a caring look before turning to the sunset and leaving. Ron narrates that Yang never stopped walking, putting as much space between him and the people he loved as possible. The scene then shifts to a hooded man in a parka. Another man approaches and the hooded man nimbly kills him, knives falling out of the latter's hands as he collapses. The hooded man, revealed to be Yang, stands up and goes to his shack, where he takes the pendant he had been given by Lynne, his sword disguised as a snowman's broom and April's pacifier before setting the hut on fire. Walking out to the snow, a slew of clan warriors leap out of the snow, and Yang unsheathes his sword as the scene fades.

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

The film was written and directed by Sngmoo Lee, and produced by [Barrie M. Osborne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrie_M._Osborne "Barrie M. Osborne") (who also produced *[The Lord of the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_\(film_series\) "The Lord of the Rings (film series)")*[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)), along with Lee Joo-Ick and [Michael Peyser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Peyser "Michael Peyser"). [Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematography "Cinematography") was by Woo-Hyung Kim, and Jonathan Woodford-Robinson edited the film. [Javier Navarrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Navarrete "Javier Navarrete") composed the score.

Filming began in [Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland") on 12 November 2007 and wrapped on 28 February 2008\.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")\]

The film received negative reviews. It has a 31% approval rating on the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), based on 42 reviews, with an average rating of 4\.5 out of 10\. The website's consensus reads, "Perfectly, thoroughly divisive, *The Warrior's Way* will either be delightful or unbearable, depending on your tolerance for surreal, shamelessly over the top collisions of eastern and western clichés."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "C−" on an A+ to F scale.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

### Box office

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Warrior%27s_Way&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Box office")\]

In the film's opening weekend, it grossed a poor $3,048,665 in the US. The film ranked \#9 at the weekend charts.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The number of theatres dramatically reduced from 1,622 to 34 within three weeks from the opening day.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The film grossed $11,087,569 worldwide and had a production budget of $42 million, making the movie a [box office bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_office_bomb "Box office bomb").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The movie was one of the biggest box office bombs of 2010 next to *[MacGruber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacGruber_\(film\) "MacGruber (film)")*, *[How Do You Know](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_You_Know "How Do You Know")* and *[Jonah Hex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hex_\(film\) "Jonah Hex (film)")*.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

***Detachment*** is a 2011 American [psychological drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_drama "Psychological drama") film directed by [Tony Kaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Kaye_\(director\) "Tony Kaye (director)") and written by Carl Lund. Its story follows Henry Barthes, a high-school [substitute teacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_teacher "Substitute teacher") who becomes a role model to his students and others. It stars [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody"), [Marcia Gay Harden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcia_Gay_Harden "Marcia Gay Harden"), [Christina Hendricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Hendricks "Christina Hendricks"), [William Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Petersen "William Petersen"), [Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston "Bryan Cranston"), [Tim Blake Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Blake_Nelson "Tim Blake Nelson"), Betty Kaye, [Sami Gayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Gayle "Sami Gayle"), [Lucy Liu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Liu "Lucy Liu"), [Blythe Danner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blythe_Danner "Blythe Danner") and [James Caan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Caan "James Caan").

Produced by [Greg Shapiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Shapiro_\(producer\) "Greg Shapiro (producer)"), Carl Lund, Bingo Gubelmann, [Austin Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Stark "Austin Stark"), Benji Kohn, and Chris Papavasiliou, the film was released on March 16, 2012, to mixed reviews.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Substitute teacher Henry Barthes is called in for a one-month assignment, teaching English classes at a high school with many students performing at a low grade level. During his first class, he observes many acts of hostility and antagonism, including two students verbally harassing pupil Meredith, with whom he becomes acquainted after class.

After school, Henry is called in to see his grandfather at a care facility, who has become confused due to his [dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dementia "Dementia"). He frequently believes Henry is Patricia (Henry's mother). On the bus ride home, Henry sees teenage runaway Erica having sex for money, then getting hit by a man who refuses to pay her. Erica attempts to convince Henry to have sex with her, which he refuses.

The next day, Henry reads aloud to the class through the essays from earlier. After reading an anonymous essay which is assumed to be Meredith's, he becomes aware of her struggles with suicidal thoughts. On the way home, Henry again runs into Erica, who he invites up to his apartment and allows her to stay temporarily.

Later, fellow teacher Sarah asks Henry out. Henry returns home late and Erica is still awake, waiting for him. She is upset that he went out without telling her, to which he informs her that she cannot expect him to tell her such things.

Henry is later called into the care facility, because his grandfather has become gravely ill. Henry pretends to be Patricia and reassures him, allowing him to come to peace with dying. After the visit, Henry and Erica go to the park, where Henry details Patricia's suicide. He also implies that his grandfather had sexually abused Patricia, but says that he never felt unsafe around either of them.

Back at school, Meredith shows Henry an artwork that she made for him. She opens up about her struggles and becomes visibly upset, hugging Henry and asking him to console her. Sarah walks in on them, causing Meredith to run away, and she accuses Henry of touching Meredith inappropriately. Henry insists that he was just comforting her, but the accusation leads to a surge of memories about his grandfather and mother. He's overcome by panic, and quickly leaves.

Later that day, Henry is informed of his grandfather's death. Feeling overwhelmed after all that's happened, Henry tells Erica he can no longer take care of her, and has social services take her to a foster home. She pleads with Henry to let her stay, but he reluctantly maintains his stance.

As Henry's assignment comes to an end, his students show their appreciation for his work. During a break, Henry tries to apologise to Meredith for what happened earlier, but she quickly dismisses the matter. She then intentionally eats a cupcake that she poisoned, ending her life. Her death leads Henry into a state of reflection, and he decides to go visit Erica in the foster care facility for the first time since they were separated. She euphorically embraces him.

On his last day of teaching, Henry reads to the class the short story "[The Fall of the House of Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_of_the_House_of_Usher "The Fall of the House of Usher")" (1839) by [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe").

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Filming took place in [Mineola Middle School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineola_Middle_School_\(New_York\) "Mineola Middle School (New York)") and [Mineola High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineola_High_School_\(New_York\) "Mineola High School (New York)") on [Long Island, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island").

In the same month, director Tony Kaye said in an interview. "My agent sent me this fantastic piece of writing by a guy called Carl Lund. A writer. One of the things that I felt was how real it was. And writing is really about research and speech and I thought this guy’s really done his homework. In fact it turned out that he had been a teacher. So then it all became very clear. And then when it really began, if you like, really really began was when Adrien Brody sort of popped up and said I'll do this. A couple of weeks before we were supposed to start to shoot. And then I decided myself at that point I'm gonna hang the whole thing on you \[Brody\]. And try to build out your character of Henry much more and make it all everything about you. Just you." The interviewer then asks Kaye if he rebuilt the script at that point. Kaye responds, "Well I reinterpreted it, yeah. When Carl first wrote it, I believe it was a very vignette ensemble thing." ”Carl's script was very impressionistic, and \[a\] part of what I do, sometimes, \[is\] very impressionistic storytelling. I used that to its full, here, to try and make sense of it all....[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) There's more \[footage\] of Marcia Gay Harden and Bryan Cranston \[which\] I've got in the hard drives, and I'm hoping to \[get\] it out, in maybe a longer cut."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")\]

*Detachment* premiered on April 25, 2011, at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival").[\[1\]](#cite_note-premiere-1) Pretty Pictures acquired rights to distribute the film in France.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) In September 2011, Tribeca Film acquired U.S. distribution rights with Celluloid Dreams repping worldwide sales rights.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Territories sold include Benelux (Wild Bunch), Italy (UBU), Middle East (Shooting Stars), Russia (CP Digital), Latin America (California), India (Pictureworks), Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam (PT Parkit) and Taiwan (Cineplex).[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

On September 9, 2011, *Detachment* screened in competition at the 37th [Deauville American Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deauville_American_Film_Festival "Deauville American Film Festival") in France.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It won both the Revelations Prize and the International Critics' Award.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) On September 18, *Detachment* was announced as the Closing Night Film at the [Woodstock Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock_Film_Festival "Woodstock Film Festival"), where Kaye was the recipient of the Honorary Maverick Award.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

On October 12, 2011, *Detachment* screened in competition at the Valenciennes International Festival of Action and Adventure Films in France, where it won the Grand Prize and the Audience Award.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Later, on October 26, the film screened in competition at the 24th [Tokyo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_International_Film_Festival "Tokyo International Film Festival").[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It received the award for Best Artistic Contribution, sharing honors with the film *Kora*.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

*Detachment* also screened in competition at the 35th [São Paulo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_International_Film_Festival "São Paulo International Film Festival") and won the Audience Award for Best Foreign Language Film, sharing honors with *[Chicken with Plums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_with_Plums_\(film\) "Chicken with Plums (film)")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) On November 16, *Detachment* screened at the 53rd Muestra Internacional de Cine in Mexico.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

In January 2012, *Detachment* won Best Picture at the Ramdam Film Festival in Tournai, Belgium.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Critical response

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Critical response")\]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film has an approval rating of 57% based on 72 reviews, with an average rating of 5\.8/10. The website's critics consensus reads: "*Detachment*'s heart is in the right place, but overall it doesn't offer any solutions to its passionate ranting."[\[18\]](#cite_note-tomatoes-18) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 52 based on reviews from 20 critics.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

[Peter Travers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Travers "Peter Travers") from *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* awarded the film three out of four stars, praising the performances of Adrien Brody, Marcia Gay Harden and Lucy Liu. "*Detachment* gets to you. It hits hard", he wrote.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

A reviewer for Student Handouts, which reviews books and films for those working in education, said: "It easily makes *[Dangerous Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Minds "Dangerous Minds")* look like a pandering [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_\(TV_network\) "Lifetime (TV network)") made-for-TV movie."[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

2011 film by Tony Kaye

Detachment

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/20/Detachment_poster.jpg/250px-Detachment_poster.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Detachment_poster.jpg)

Written by | Carl Lund

Produced by | - [Greg Shapiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Shapiro_\(producer\) "Greg Shapiro (producer)") - Carl Lund - Bingo Gubelmann - [Austin Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Stark "Austin Stark") - Benji Kohn - Chris Papavasiliou

Distributed by | [Tribeca Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Films "Tribeca Films")

Release dates | - April 25, 2011 (2011-04-25) (Tribeca)[\[1\]](#cite_note-premiere-1) - March 16, 2012 (2012-03-16) (United States)

***Detachment*** is a 2011 American [psychological drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_drama "Psychological drama") film directed by [Tony Kaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Kaye_\(director\) "Tony Kaye (director)") and written by Carl Lund. Its story follows Henry Barthes, a high-school [substitute teacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_teacher "Substitute teacher") who becomes a role model to his students and others. It stars [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody"), [Marcia Gay Harden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcia_Gay_Harden "Marcia Gay Harden"), [Christina Hendricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Hendricks "Christina Hendricks"), [William Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Petersen "William Petersen"), [Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston "Bryan Cranston"), [Tim Blake Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Blake_Nelson "Tim Blake Nelson"), Betty Kaye, [Sami Gayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Gayle "Sami Gayle"), [Lucy Liu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Liu "Lucy Liu"), [Blythe Danner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blythe_Danner "Blythe Danner") and [James Caan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Caan "James Caan").

Produced by [Greg Shapiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Shapiro_\(producer\) "Greg Shapiro (producer)"), Carl Lund, Bingo Gubelmann, [Austin Stark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Stark "Austin Stark"), Benji Kohn, and Chris Papavasiliou, the film was released on March 16, 2012, to mixed reviews.

## Plot

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")\]

Substitute teacher Henry Barthes is called in for a one-month assignment, teaching English classes at a high school with many students performing at a low grade level. During his first class, he observes many acts of hostility and antagonism, including two students verbally harassing pupil Meredith, with whom he becomes acquainted after class.

After school, Henry is called in to see his grandfather at a care facility, who has become confused due to his [dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dementia "Dementia"). He frequently believes Henry is Patricia (Henry's mother). On the bus ride home, Henry sees teenage runaway Erica having sex for money, then getting hit by a man who refuses to pay her. Erica attempts to convince Henry to have sex with her, which he refuses.

The next day, Henry reads aloud to the class through the essays from earlier. After reading an anonymous essay which is assumed to be Meredith's, he becomes aware of her struggles with suicidal thoughts. On the way home, Henry again runs into Erica, who he invites up to his apartment and allows her to stay temporarily.

Later, fellow teacher Sarah asks Henry out. Henry returns home late and Erica is still awake, waiting for him. She is upset that he went out without telling her, to which he informs her that she cannot expect him to tell her such things.

Henry is later called into the care facility, because his grandfather has become gravely ill. Henry pretends to be Patricia and reassures him, allowing him to come to peace with dying. After the visit, Henry and Erica go to the park, where Henry details Patricia's suicide. He also implies that his grandfather had sexually abused Patricia, but says that he never felt unsafe around either of them.

Back at school, Meredith shows Henry an artwork that she made for him. She opens up about her struggles and becomes visibly upset, hugging Henry and asking him to console her. Sarah walks in on them, causing Meredith to run away, and she accuses Henry of touching Meredith inappropriately. Henry insists that he was just comforting her, but the accusation leads to a surge of memories about his grandfather and mother. He's overcome by panic, and quickly leaves.

Later that day, Henry is informed of his grandfather's death. Feeling overwhelmed after all that's happened, Henry tells Erica he can no longer take care of her, and has social services take her to a foster home. She pleads with Henry to let her stay, but he reluctantly maintains his stance.

As Henry's assignment comes to an end, his students show their appreciation for his work. During a break, Henry tries to apologise to Meredith for what happened earlier, but she quickly dismisses the matter. She then intentionally eats a cupcake that she poisoned, ending her life. Her death leads Henry into a state of reflection, and he decides to go visit Erica in the foster care facility for the first time since they were separated. She euphorically embraces him.

On his last day of teaching, Henry reads to the class the short story "[The Fall of the House of Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_of_the_House_of_Usher "The Fall of the House of Usher")" (1839) by [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe").

## Cast

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast")\]

- [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody") as Henry Barthes

- [Marcia Gay Harden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcia_Gay_Harden "Marcia Gay Harden") as Principal Carol Dearden

- [William Petersen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Petersen "William Petersen") as Mr. Sarge Kepler

## Production

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")\]

Filming took place in [Mineola Middle School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineola_Middle_School_\(New_York\) "Mineola Middle School (New York)") and [Mineola High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineola_High_School_\(New_York\) "Mineola High School (New York)") on [Long Island, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island").

In the same month, director Tony Kaye said in an interview. "My agent sent me this fantastic piece of writing by a guy called Carl Lund. A writer. One of the things that I felt was how real it was. And writing is really about research and speech and I thought this guy’s really done his homework. In fact it turned out that he had been a teacher. So then it all became very clear. And then when it really began, if you like, really really began was when Adrien Brody sort of popped up and said I'll do this. A couple of weeks before we were supposed to start to shoot. And then I decided myself at that point I'm gonna hang the whole thing on you \[Brody\]. And try to build out your character of Henry much more and make it all everything about you. Just you." The interviewer then asks Kaye if he rebuilt the script at that point. Kaye responds, "Well I reinterpreted it, yeah. When Carl first wrote it, I believe it was a very vignette ensemble thing." ”Carl's script was very impressionistic, and \[a\] part of what I do, sometimes, \[is\] very impressionistic storytelling. I used that to its full, here, to try and make sense of it all....[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) There's more \[footage\] of Marcia Gay Harden and Bryan Cranston \[which\] I've got in the hard drives, and I'm hoping to \[get\] it out, in maybe a longer cut."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Release")\]

*Detachment* premiered on April 25, 2011, at the [Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Film_Festival "Tribeca Film Festival").[\[1\]](#cite_note-premiere-1) Pretty Pictures acquired rights to distribute the film in France.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) In September 2011, Tribeca Film acquired U.S. distribution rights with Celluloid Dreams repping worldwide sales rights.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Territories sold include Benelux (Wild Bunch), Italy (UBU), Middle East (Shooting Stars), Russia (CP Digital), Latin America (California), India (Pictureworks), Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam (PT Parkit) and Taiwan (Cineplex).[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

On September 9, 2011, *Detachment* screened in competition at the 37th [Deauville American Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deauville_American_Film_Festival "Deauville American Film Festival") in France.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It won both the Revelations Prize and the International Critics' Award.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) On September 18, *Detachment* was announced as the Closing Night Film at the [Woodstock Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock_Film_Festival "Woodstock Film Festival"), where Kaye was the recipient of the Honorary Maverick Award.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

On October 12, 2011, *Detachment* screened in competition at the Valenciennes International Festival of Action and Adventure Films in France, where it won the Grand Prize and the Audience Award.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Later, on October 26, the film screened in competition at the 24th [Tokyo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_International_Film_Festival "Tokyo International Film Festival").[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It received the award for Best Artistic Contribution, sharing honors with the film *Kora*.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

*Detachment* also screened in competition at the 35th [São Paulo International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_International_Film_Festival "São Paulo International Film Festival") and won the Audience Award for Best Foreign Language Film, sharing honors with *[Chicken with Plums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_with_Plums_\(film\) "Chicken with Plums (film)")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) On November 16, *Detachment* screened at the 53rd Muestra Internacional de Cine in Mexico.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

In January 2012, *Detachment* won Best Picture at the Ramdam Film Festival in Tournai, Belgium.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Critical response

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Detachment_\(film\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Critical response")\]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film has an approval rating of 57% based on 72 reviews, with an average rating of 5\.8/10. The website's critics consensus reads: "*Detachment*'s heart is in the right place, but overall it doesn't offer any solutions to its passionate ranting."[\[18\]](#cite_note-tomatoes-18) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a weighted average score of 52 based on reviews from 20 critics.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

[Peter Travers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Travers "Peter Travers") from *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* awarded the film three out of four stars, praising the performances of Adrien Brody, Marcia Gay Harden and Lucy Liu. "*Detachment* gets to you. It hits hard", he wrote.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

A reviewer for Student Handouts, which reviews books and films for those working in education, said: "It easily makes *[Dangerous Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Minds "Dangerous Minds")* look like a pandering [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_\(TV_network\) "Lifetime (TV network)") made-for-TV movie."[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

python3 << 'EOF'
from PIL import Image
import colorsys
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
W,H = im.size
px = im.load()
cols=[]
for x in range(W):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(H):
        p=px[x,y]; r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r/H,g/H,b/H))

import statistics
def hsv(c):
    r,g,b=[v/255 for v in c]
    h,l,s=colorsys.rgb_to_hls(r,g,b)
    return h,l,s
sats=[hsv(c)[2] for c in cols]
hues=[hsv(c)[0] for c in cols]
print("mean sat:", sum(sats)/len(sats))
print("median sat:", statistics.median(sats))
# luminance profile per 5% block
print("\nLuminance & sat per 5% block (x range avg):")
for i in range(20):
    a,b0=int(W*i/20),int(W*(i+1)/20)
    l=[0.299*c[0]+0.587*c[1]+0.114*c[2] for c in cols[a:b0]]
    s=[hsv(c)[2] for c in cols[a:b0]]
    h=[hsv(c)[0]*360 for c in cols[a:b0]]
    # dominant hue among saturated cols
    hh=[x for x,s0 in zip(h,s) if s0>0.15]
    hh_desc = f"{sum(hh)/len(hh):.0f}deg" if hh else "-"
    print(f"block {i:2d} [{a:4d},{b0:4d})  lum={sum(l)/len(l):6.1f}  sat={sum(s)/len(s):.3f}  domHue={hh_desc}")

# very bright stripes (white-ish)
print("\nNear-white stripes lum>150:")
wb=[(x,cols[x]) for x in range(W) if 0.299*cols[x][0]+0.587*cols[x][1]+0.114*cols[x][2]>150]
print(wb[:30])
EOF

for x in range(W):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(H):

def stats(vectors, label=""):
    # vectors: list of flat RGB tuples
    lums=[]; sats=[]; hues=[]
    hist=[0]*64  # 4x4x4
    for v in vectors:
        r,g,b = v[0]/255, v[1]/255, v[2]/255
        l=(0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b)
        h,l2,s=colorsys.rgb_to_hls(r,g,b)
        lums.append(l); sats.append(s); hues.append(h*360)
        bi=min(3,int(r*4)); gi=min(3,int(g*4)); bi2=min(3,int(b*4))
        hist[bi*16+gi*4+bi2]+=1
    n=len(vectors)

    # warm fraction hue 0..60
    warm=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and (h<60 or h>340))/n

    green=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and 70<h<170)/n
    return dict(lum=sum(lums)/n, medlum=statistics.median(lums), sat=sum(sats)/n,

def hist_from_cols(cols_):
    return stats(cols_)

def cos(a,b):
    na=(sum(x*x for x in a))**0.5; nb=(sum(x*x for x in b))**0.5
    return sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))/(na*nb) if na and nb else 0

import urllib.request, json, urllib.parse, io, os
from PIL import Image

def get(u):
    req=urllib.request.Request(u, headers={'User-Agent':'Mozilla/5.0'})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read()

def thumbs_for(ident):
    m=json.loads(get(f"https://archive.org/metadata/{ident}").decode('utf8','ignore'))
    names=[f['name'] for f in m.get('files',[]) if '.thumbs/' in f.get('name','') and f.get('format') in (None,'JPEG','JPEG Image','JPEG Thumb')]
    if not names:
        names=[f['name'] for f in m.get('files',[]) if '.thumbs/' in f.get('name','')]
    names=sorted(names, key=lambda n: int(n.rsplit('_',1)[1].split('.')[0]))
    out=[]
    for n in names:
        u=f"https://archive.org/download/{ident}/"+urllib.parse.quote(n)
        try:
            data=get(u)
            img=Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)).convert('RGB')
            out.append((n, img))
        except Exception as e:
            print("  fail", n, repr(e)[:80])
    return out

for ident in ["2011-detachment-tony-kaye-eu"]:
    th=thumbs_for(ident)
    print(ident, "thumbs:", len(th))
    for name,img in th[:3]:
        print("  ", name, img.size)
    # save for later analysis
    imgs=[(n, i) for n,i in th]
    means=[]
    for n,img in imgs:
        small=img.resize((32,18))
        px=list(small.getdata())
        r=sum(p[0] for p in px)/len(px); g=sum(p[1] for p in px)/len(px); b=sum(p[2] for p in px)/len(px)
        means.append((n,(r,g,b)))
    json.dump({n:m for n,m in means}, open(f"/tmp/ia/{ident}_means.json","w"))
    # build barcode image
    bc=Image.new('RGB',(len(imgs),60))
    for i,(n,m) in enumerate(means):
        col=tuple(min(255,int(v)) for v in m)
        for y in range(60): bc.putpixel((i,y),col)
    bc.save(f"/tmp/ia/{ident}_barcode.png")
    print("  saved barcode", len(means))

import urllib.request, json, urllib.parse, io

def thumbs_for(ident):
    m=json.loads(get(f"https://archive.org/metadata/{ident}").decode('utf8','ignore'))

    names=sorted(names, key=lambda n: int(n.rsplit('_',1)[1].split('.')[0]))
    out=[]
    for n in names:
        try:
            data=get(f"https://archive.org/download/{ident}/"+urllib.parse.quote(n))
            img=Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)).convert('RGB')
            out.append(img)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return out

def stats_from_imgs(imgs):
    lums=[]; sats=[]; hues=[]; hist=[0]*64
    for img in imgs:
        small=img.resize((32,18))
        px=list(small.getdata())
        r=sum(p[0] for p in px)/len(px); g=sum(p[1] for p in px)/len(px); b=sum(p[2] for p in px)/len(px)
        r0,g0,b0=r/255,g/255,b/255
        l=0.299*r0+0.587*g0+0.114*b0
        h,l2,s=colorsys.rgb_to_hls(r0,g0,b0)
        lums.append(l); sats.append(s); hues.append(h*360)
        hist[min(3,int(r0*4))*16+min(3,int(g0*4))*4+min(3,int(b0*4))]+=1
    n=len(imgs); hist=[c/n for c in hist]
    warm=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and (h<60 or h>340))/n
    blue=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and 180<h<260)/n
    green=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and 70<h<170)/n
    return dict(lum=sum(lums)/n, sat=sum(sats)/n, warm=warm, blue=blue, green=green,
                dark=sum(1 for l in lums if l<0.12)/n, pale=sum(1 for l in lums if l>0.5)/n, hist=hist)

def cos(a,b):
    na=sum(x*x for x in a)**0.5; nb=sum(x*x for x in b)**0.5
    return sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))/(na*nb) if na and nb else 0

# target content-only columns

tcols=[]
for x in range(W):

    for y in range(H):
        p=px[x,y]; r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    tcols.append((r/H,g/H,b/H))
def stats_from_cols(vs):

        hist[min(3,int(r0*4))*16+min(3,int(g0*4))*4+min(3,int(b0*4))]+=1
    n=len(vs); hist=[c/n for c in hist]
    warm=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and (h<60 or h>340))/n
    blue=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and 180<h<260)/n
    green=sum(1 for h,s in zip(hues,sats) if s>0.12 and 70<h<170)/n
    return dict(lum=sum(lums)/n,sat=sum(sats)/n,warm=warm,blue=blue,green=green,

## Analysis Summary

**Target barcode** (1000 cols; ~93% film + ~7% black credits): extremely muted warm browns/grays/olives, mean luminance 0.22, mean saturation 0.20, **zero** near-white, ~11% near-black, tiny blue fraction (2%), dominated by warm hues (71%).

**Leaves of Grass (2009)** — built from archive.org preview frames (1/min, full film):
- Color-histogram cosine similarity to target: **0.987** (best of all candidates; Detachment: 0.860)
- Palette stats nearly identical: lum 0.22 vs 0.22, warm 0.67 vs 0.71, blue 0.04 vs 0.03, pale 0.00 vs 0.00
- **Distinctive saturated blue stripe at 42–44% of runtime in both** (the single most salient color event in the target)
- **Secondary blue-gray blip at ~48.5% in both**
- **Credits start at exactly 93%** in both (target col 930/1000; Leaves frame 94/101), with matching black tails
- Opening black frame at x=0–3 ↔ Leaves frame 0 black
- Dark blue-gray dip at ~71–75% in both

**Why not Detachment (C)**, the aesthetic runner-up: its full-film palette is much cooler/gray (warm 0.41 vs 0.71), **has no blue stripe at all** (blue 0.00 vs target 0.03), is less saturated (0.144 vs 0.202), and has pale/bright frames (0.06) absent in the target. The trailers fooled me initially — trailers oversample colorful scenes — but the full-film data settled it. Other candidates (rom-coms like The Rebound, Georgia Rule, The Accidental Husband) are far brighter with pale/white regions the target lacks; The Warrior's Way is heavily blue/teal throughout.
